CVE-2026-41850 is an algorithmic denial-of-service in Spring SpEL that requires the application to evaluate a specially crafted expression supplied by an attacker. PingAccess does not evaluate SpEL expressions from external or user-controlled sources, so the vulnerable execution path is not reachable. The spring-expression-5.3.33.jar is present in the distribution and contains the SpEL implementation, so the scanner's dependency finding is valid; however, library presence alone does not establish exploitability. Engineering has tracked dependency remediation under PA-16550 and plans to upgrade the Spring dependency in a future PingAccess release. Not exploitable in PingAccess. CVE-2026-46595 affects the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh SSH server implementation (versions below 0.52.0, fixed in 0.52.0): a server whose VerifiedPublicKeyCallback returns a source-address restriction in Permissions.CriticalOptions fails to enforce that restriction, allowing an authenticated key holder connecting from a disallowed address to complete authentication. Exploitation requires a network-reachable x/crypto/ssh-based SSH server with that callback configuration. The PingAccess Docker image (9.0.3) contains no SSH server of any kind and exposes no SSH port (only PA engine/admin ports 1443, 3000, 9000). The scanner finding matches the git-lfs utility bundled in the image, which declares x/crypto 0.51.0 in its Go module manifest; however, the x/crypto/ssh package and its affected symbols are not compiled into the git-lfs binary at all (only unrelated md4/pbkdf2 code is present), and git-lfs uses the system OpenSSH client for SSH transport. The vulnerable code is therefore absent from the image and the required server-side execution context does not exist. This is a false positive. The manifest-level finding will clear when the bundled git-lfs is built against x/crypto 0.52.0 or later in a future image refresh.

Not exploitable in PingAccess 9.1. CVE-2026-54704 affects the OpenTelemetry JDBC auto-instrumentation prior to 2.28.0, which can fail to sanitize double-quoted passwords in SQL CONNECT statements, potentially exposing clear-text database passwords in exported trace span attributes. The OpenTelemetry javaagent bundled in the pingaccess:2607-9.1.0 image (2.24.0, JDBC instrumentation 2.24.0-alpha - within the affected range) is not attached to the JVM by default: the image launch script passes no -javaagent argument and the default run.properties ships pa.enable.distributed.tracing=false. The instrumentation only activates if an administrator explicitly enables distributed tracing. The vulnerable pattern also requires credentials embedded directly in SQL statement text (e.g. CONNECT ... PASSWORD ...); PingAccess authenticates to its data stores through JDBC connection configuration rather than SQL statement text. A library upgrade of the bundled OpenTelemetry agent to a release at or above 2.28.0 is planned for a future maintenance release.

Multiple Netty releases bundled in maintenance versions of PingAccess 8.3.x contain the vulnerable library (CVE-2026-89044 - HTTP request smuggling via malformed Transfer-Encoding declarations). PingAccess does not invoke the SpEL API in any production code path, so no attacker-supplied input can reach expression evaluation. Spring refresh scheduled with the library upgrades in PingAccess 9.2.

PingAccess 8.3 bundles Netty versions within the affected range (4.1.118 in 8.3.0; 4.1.132 in 8.3.x maintenance builds). The chunk-size line-terminator parsing flaw is present, but PingAccess is a parse-and-re-encode proxy: the front-end decoder parses inbound requests and the backend encoder re-serializes them with strict CRLF framing to the origin, so no desynchronized byte stream reaches the origin. Exploitability is limited to deployments where PingAccess sits behind another proxy that parses chunk framing differently. PingAccess 8.3.6 bundles Netty 4.1.138, which is outside the affected range.

PingAccess 8.3 bundles Netty versions within the affected range (4.1.118 in 8.3.0; fixed in 4.1.132, which 8.3.x maintenance builds ship). The quoted-string chunk-extension parsing flaw is present in 8.3.0, but PingAccess is a parse-and-re-encode proxy: inbound requests are parsed by the front-end decoder and re-serialized with canonical CRLF framing to the origin, so chunk-extension ambiguities are not forwarded to the origin byte stream. PingAccess 8.3.6 bundles Netty 4.1.138, outside the affected range.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The flaw requires application code to call setUri() with unvalidated attacker-controlled input after constructing a DefaultHttpRequest, bypassing the request-line validation that constructors apply. In PingAccess the outbound origin request URI is derived from the inbound request-line, which Netty's HttpObjectDecoder validates during parsing (CRLF and whitespace are rejected); PingAccess does not construct DefaultHttpRequest objects with post-validation attacker-controlled URIs on the proxy path. No CRLF injection path exists.

PingAccess 8.3 bundles Netty versions within the affected range (4.1.118 in 8.3.0; 4.1.132 in 8.3.x maintenance builds). The chunk-size integer-overflow parsing flaw is present, but PingAccess is a parse-and-re-encode proxy: inbound chunk framing is parsed by the front-end decoder and re-serialized with correct sizes and strict CRLF framing to the origin, so an overflow-induced framing ambiguity is not forwarded to the origin. Exploitability is limited to deployments where PingAccess sits behind another proxy that parses chunk framing differently. PingAccess 8.3.6 bundles Netty 4.1.138, outside the affected range.

PingAccess 8.3 bundles Netty versions within the affected range (4.1.118 in 8.3.0; 4.1.132 in 8.3.x maintenance builds). The HTTP/1.0 Transfer-Encoding plus Content-Length coexistence flaw is reachable: PingAccess's front-end decoder hard-rejects the conflicting-header combination only for HTTP/1.1, and HTTP/1.0 requests bypass that guard. Impact is limited because PingAccess is a parse-and-re-encode proxy, not a byte-forwarder: the request is decoded and re-serialized to the origin, so no second parser sees the ambiguous byte stream. PingAccess 8.3.6 bundles Netty 4.1.138, outside the affected range.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The flaw is in Netty's Lz4FrameDecoder, a standalone codec handler that must be explicitly added to a channel pipeline. PingAccess never adds LZ4 handlers to any pipeline: its compression handling uses HttpContentDecompressor (gzip/deflate/br/zstd/snappy for origin-response rewriting) and its own content layers; no Lz4FrameDecoder or EmbeddedLz4xx decoder is registered anywhere in the PingAccess distribution.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The flaw is in Netty's HttpClientCodec, which pairs outbound requests with inbound responses via a queue poll. PingAccess does not use HttpClientCodec: the backend channel uses PingAccess's own BackEndHttpRequestEncoder and BackEndHttpResponseDecoder pair, whose response-to-request association is implemented separately. The vulnerable polling logic is not in the product's pipeline.

PingAccess 8.3 bundles Netty versions within the affected range (4.1.118 in 8.3.0; 4.1.132 in 8.3.x maintenance builds). The malformed Transfer-Encoding parsing flaw is present, but PingAccess is a parse-and-re-encode proxy: inbound requests are decoded and re-serialized with canonical framing to the origin, and the front-end decoder hard-rejects conflicting Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length combinations on HTTP/1.1. Exploitability is limited to deployments where PingAccess sits behind another proxy that parses Transfer-Encoding differently. PingAccess 8.3.6 bundles Netty 4.1.138, outside the affected range.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The flaw bypasses the optional maxAllocation limit of Netty's HttpContentDecompressor for br/zstd/snappy encodings. PingAccess instantiates HttpContentDecompressor with no maxAllocation configured (default constructor), so there is no limit to bypass, and the decompressor is applied only to responses from the customer's own origin servers (backend response rewriting), not to attacker-controlled inbound requests.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The flaw concerns hostname verification when TLS-configured Socket or Syslog appenders are used. The shipped log4j2.xml contains no active Socket/Syslog appenders (all network appender definitions are commented out) and no <Ssl> configuration or verifyHostName attribute appears anywhere in the shipped configuration; the only active layouts are file/console/database appenders with PatternLayout and JsonTemplateLayout. The vulnerable configuration path is not present. Log4j 2.25.4 (fix) ships in PingAccess 8.3.6.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The flaw is log injection via CRLF in the Rfc5424Layout (syslog) when configured directly with TCP framing. Rfc5424Layout does not appear anywhere in PingAccess's shipped log4j2.xml; audit-to-syslog appenders use other layouts and are disabled by default (all network appenders are commented out). The vulnerable configuration is not present. Log4j 2.25.4 (fix) ships in PingAccess 8.3.6.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The flaw is silent log-event loss/malformed XML in XmlLayout when log messages contain XML 1.0 forbidden characters. PingAccess 8.3 bundles Netty 4.1.118, within the affected range (4.1.x <= 4.1.136). The mechanism is reachable in PingAccess through PingAccess's own front-end response encoder (FrontEndHttpResponseEncoder), which pairs responses to pipelined requests via a method queue and polls it once per outbound response without excluding 1xx informational responses - the same pattern described in the upstream advisory for HttpServerCodec. PingAccess answers Expect: 100-continue automatically by default, so a pipelined GET (Expect: 100-continue) followed by HEAD can mispair the queue and desynchronize response framing on the client-facing connection. Impact is bounded: PingAccess is a parse-and-re-encode proxy, so no desynchronized request stream reaches the origin servers, and the effect is limited to the attacker's own connection. This behavior is independent of the bundled Netty version and is tracked as a product fix under PA-16719; upgrading the bundled Netty alone does not remediate it.

PingAccess 8.3 bundles jackson-core 2.17.0, at the boundary of the affected range (the flaw was introduced in exactly 2.17.0). The vulnerable method (NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber) runs when Jackson deserializes a JSON string into a numeric-typed field with attacker-controlled length. PingAccess does not deserialize untrusted client request bodies via Jackson into typed objects - inbound request bodies are proxied, not bound. The JSON PingAccess parses comes from the configured, trusted token provider (RFC 7662 introspection responses, PingFederate, PingOne) or from PA-signed/-encrypted structures (the OIDC state JSON is JWE-protected, so clients cannot inject arbitrary content). No unauthenticated-attacker path to numeric-string coercion exists; the library refresh ships in an upcoming maintenance release.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The vulnerable method (UTF8DataInputJsonParser._reportInvalidToken) is only reachable through parsers created from a java.io.DataInput source (JsonFactory.createParser(DataInput)). PingAccess contains exactly one such call site: the Java-serialization readObject() of its internal ImmutableJsonNode type, used for cluster-internal object transfer - not an HTTP input path. No attacker-controlled JSON reaches a DataInput-based parser, and the unbounded error-token accumulation cannot be triggered.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The deserializer-cache growth requires name-based polymorphic deserialization (JSON type IDs resolving through a default implementation) with attacker-controlled type identifiers. PingAccess does not use polymorphic type handling: no @JsonTypeInfo/@JsonSubTypes annotations, no activateDefaultTyping/enableDefaultTyping, and no ObjectMapper configuration that enables type resolution - verified across the engine and admin code. The required deserialization feature does not exist in the product.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The quadratic forward-reference resolution requires deserializing attacker-controlled JSON into @JsonIdentityInfo-enabled collections or maps. PingAccess uses no @JsonIdentityInfo annotations anywhere, and its deserialization targets are specific response bean types (from trusted token providers) or plain JsonNode trees, which do not perform object-ID reference resolution.

Affected range confirmed - the fix ships in bc-fips 2.0.2, and PingAccess bundles 2.0.0. Impact is limited: the finalize()-based zeroisation flaw means key material processed by the BCFIPS provider can linger in the heap via the pending-finalizer queue (and contribute to OOM under sustained load); recovering the material requires local access to the process or a heap dump - there is no remote attack path. Exposure in PingAccess is limited to FIPS-mode deployments: the startup script places resource/bc/fips/* on the classpath only when pa.fips.mode=true in conf/fips-mode.properties; default (non-FIPS) deployments load resource/bc/non-fips (bcprov, not the affected BCFIPS library). The scanned path tools/csd/ is the collect-support-data utility, which runs on demand and is not part of the server runtime classpath. The library will be refreshed in an upcoming maintenance release. Tracking: PA-16720.

Not affected. The vulnerable branch is FromStringDeserializer's InetAddress type binding; PingAccess does not deserialize JSON into InetAddress/URL-typed fields anywhere - verified across all readValue call sites in the engine and admin code. The vulnerable code path is not reachable. Clears with the Jackson refresh tracked under PA-16721.

Not exploitable in PingAccess. The vulnerable path binds a JSON string to a javax.xml.datatype.Duration or XMLGregorianCalendar field, passing the raw string to DatatypeFactory where parsing is quadratic in digit count. PingAccess binds no javax.xml.datatype fields from JSON anywhere - verified zero references to javax.xml.datatype across all PingAccess jars; its deserialization targets use java.time, String, and numeric types. The deserializer is registered by default in jackson-databind but is never invoked because no bound type declares those fields. Clears with the Jackson refresh tracked under PA-16721.

Not affected. The vulnerability is an open-redirect in Spring Framework's UrlHandlerFilter, provided by the spring-web artifact. PingAccess does not ship spring-web (or spring-webmvc/spring-webflux) in any release - the Spring stack bundled with PingAccess is limited to the core/data/JPA modules for admin persistence, verified in 9.1.0 and 9.1.1 (a class-level scan of the distribution finds no UrlHandlerFilter). The scan attributed the finding to spring-core-6.2.17.jar because 6.2.17 falls within the affected Spring Framework version range, but the vulnerable artifact is not present in the product, so the finding is a false positive due to package attribution. The bundled Spring version will be refreshed (6.2.20+) in the 9.2 release as standard dependency hygiene.

Not affected. The vulnerability is in jackson-core's non-blocking (async) parser API; PingAccess does not use NonBlockingJsonParser, createNonBlockingByteArrayParser/ByteBufferParser, or AsyncInputFeeder anywhere in its code - only the standard synchronous parser. The vulnerable code path is unreachable. Jackson core will be refreshed in an upcoming maintenance release.

Not affected. The vulnerability is in the Bouncy Castle MLS implementation (org.bouncycastle.mls) X.509 credential handling. The org.bouncycastle.mls package is not present in the bcpkix-jdk15on-1.70.jar shipped with PingAccess (zero mls classes in the jar) and PingAccess has no MLS functionality.

Not affected. The vulnerability is in CMSAuthenticatedDataParser (streaming CMS AuthenticatedData authAttrs handling). Not affected. The vulnerable PKIXCertPathReviewer class fails to enforce X.509 NameConstraints on the leaf certificate, but only when an application uses that class for trust decisions. The class is bundled inside bcprov-jdk15on-1.70.jar (note: in bcprov, not bcpkix as the scan path suggested), however PingAccess never calls it - certificate path validation uses the JDK java.security.cert.CertPathValidator with PKIXParameters (com.pingidentity.pa.certmgmt.util.X509CertPathValidationHelper).

Not affected. CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Node.js built-in Brotli decoder, exploitable only where a Node.js runtime decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. PingAccess does not ship or execute a Node.js runtime: the Node.js-built UI is compiled ahead of time into static JavaScript bundles served by the product, and at request time the browser (not Node.js) renders it and performs any Content-Encoding decompression using the browser's own Brotli implementation, which is separate code and not affected by this CVE. Node.js is used only in CI build containers, which are not deployed to production.

Not affected. GHSA-mhm7-754m-9p8w (jackson-databind @JsonView creator-property bypass, no CVE assigned, Moderate) allows attacker-controlled JSON to populate a constructor parameter restricted with @JsonView when that parameter is also bound via @JsonTypeInfo(include = As.EXTERNAL_PROPERTY). Exploitation requires all three annotations combined in application code: a property-based @JsonCreator, a @JsonView-restricted creator parameter, and an EXTERNAL_PROPERTY type binding on that parameter. Verified across the full PingAccess 9.1 distribution (all 165 runtime jars and 83 upgrade-utility jars, class-by-class): zero PingAccess classes reference @JsonView or As.EXTERNAL_PROPERTY; the 30 classes using @JsonCreator never combine it with views or external type ids; the only @JsonTypeInfo usage is include = As.PROPERTY in pf-admin-api-clients-v2 model classes with no view restrictions. PingAccess also does not deserialize client request bodies into typed bean graphs (no spring-web/spring-webmvc in the distribution; JSON parsing is limited to trusted sources - token providers, JWE-protected structures, cluster-internal channels). The OpenTelemetry agent jar bundles its own shaded, classloader-isolated jackson 2.22.2 for internal telemetry export, which is above the affected line and does not process product data. All code-level preconditions are absent, so the vulnerable deserialization path cannot be constructed regardless of library version. Remediation rides the standard Jackson library update cadence (fixed in 2.21.5).

Not exploitable in default (non-FIPS) deployments; exposed only in FIPS-mode deployments for outbound TLS to servers presenting SAN-less certificates. CVE-2026-59638 (CVSSv4 9.3) enables Bouncy Castle's documented-as-opt-in CN fallback in the JSSE hostname verifier by default when the property is unset: a certificate without a dNSName SAN can be accepted against its Common Name. PingAccess loads the Bouncy Castle JSSE provider (bctls) only when running in FIPS mode (pa.fips.mode=true) - default non-FIPS TLS uses the JDK/Netty providers. In FIPS mode, PA registers BouncyCastleJsseProvider as the TLS provider, so outbound connections that validate SAN-less certificates use the vulnerable fallback. Mitigation without an upgrade: add -Dorg.bouncycastle.jsse.hostnameCheck.cnFallback=false to JVM options. Fix ships in bctls-fips 2.0.24 / bctls-jdk18on 1.85; PingAccess refresh tracked under PA-16751.

Not affected. CVE-2026-59639 (CVSS 8.7) allows CMS/PKCS#7 SignedData objects containing zero signer records to pass verifySignatures() as authentic - exploitable only where an application parses untrusted CMS SignedData and relies on Bouncy Castle's bulk verification as an authorization control. PingAccess does not use the CMS API anywhere: no class in the distribution references org.bouncycastle.cms (verified across all 165 runtime jars of PA 9.1.1). PingAccess uses bcpkix solely for certificate operations (X.509 parsing via org.bouncycastle.cert, CSR generation via org.bouncycastle.pkcs/PKCS10, PEM import/export via org.bouncycastle.openssl) - no SignedData parsing or verification exists in the product. Fix ships in bcpkix-fips 2.0.12 / bcpkix-jdk18on 1.85; library refresh tracked under PA-16751.

Affected (availability-only). netty-handler 4.1.135.Final is below the fix floor 4.1.137.Final and the PingAccess front-channel TLS path installs Netty's SniHandler when SNI termination is in use, so an unauthenticated client sending fragmented ClientHello records can drive quadratic CPU work before the handshake completes. No confidentiality or integrity impact. Fixed by upgrading PingAccess 8.3.5 to 8.3.6, which ships netty-handler 4.1.138.Final.
